2.text: fire, cut into pieces, and thrown into the blood. The guts are also chopped

3.text: and thrown into the blood. The same is done with fish-heads and such bits

4.text: of meat as are not consumed immediately. This mixture does not readily

5.text: become putrid, on account of the fermentation that is going on in the blood.

6.text: Bags filled with fermented blood, and putrid meat of slaughtered or dead

7.text: animals, are stored up by thrifty families for winter use. These stores are

8.text: gradually consumed during the cold season, although the Chukchee prefer to

9.text: use fresh meat, and sell them at a low price to the Russians for dog-food.

10.text: The Maritime Chukchee store away bags of seal-blood prepared in the

11.text: same manner, but their supply is not so abundant as that of the reindeer-

12.text: breeders. Walrus-meat, whale-skin, and the like, are cut into square pieces

13.text: and stored in underground cellars. Whole carcasses of seals and walruses

14.text: are often stored for several months, and afterwards eaten or used for dog-food,

15.text: although they generally become quite putrid. Blubber is stored in bags. Oil

16.text: is extracted from chopped or pounded blubber by protracted boiling. The

17.text: blubber is not chewed, as is done by the Central Eskimo in America.

18.text: In spring, about the middle of April, the Reindeer Chukchee dry some

19.text: of their meat in the open air. Under the combined action of the warm

20.text: breezes of noon and the frost of night, quite large pieces become thoroughly

21.text: dry, and keep much of their savor and softness. The dried meat is slightly

22.text: smoked over the hearth in the tent. Unlike the Lamut and the Yukaghir,

23.text: the Reindeer Chukchee do not care to dry meat in summer, because at that

24.text: season the meat must be cut into thin strips and strung on lines, which is

25.text: considered too much work. The Maritime people dry some seal-meat in

26.text: summer. It is sliced thin and hung on long poles, which form a drying-rack.

27.text: Whenever a whale drifts ashore, quantities of whale-meat are sliced thin and

28.text: hung on poles or strung on lines, or, if the weather is favorable, spread on

29.text: skins or on dry smooth rocks. The Chukchee fishermen at the mouth of the

30.text: Anadyr dry their fish on racks made in imitation of those of their neighbors,

32.text: The drying is done very carelessly. The meat or fish is seldom protected

33.text: from rain. It becomes soft, and so full of maggots that often they can be

34.text: gathered by the handful on the ground below. When it is at last dry, it is

35.text: as hard as wood, and almost as tasteless.

36.text: TABOOS. — There are several restrictions connected with animal food.

37.text: The Reindeer Chukchee abstain from the meat of the wolverene and black

38.text: bear, of all the species of Canis, and of most birds of prey. The large owl

39.text: of the tundra (Strix nyctea) and its large eggs are eaten. Milt of reindeer is

40.text: supposed to cause the impotency of men and the flabby breasts of women,

41.text: and is tabooed for young people of both sexes. The same taboo exists con-

42.text: cerning the tongue and the gastrocnemius muscle of the sacrificed fawn.
